analysis:
Examined the head excerpts of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift (about lines 1719-2634) and the ClusterOnboardingPairServing.swift patch. The PR adds a stop counter (`stopsAsked`, per the file_changes patch excerpt) to the cluster onboarding UX. The leader's status reply now carries `stopsAsked` via `followerStatus` (patch hunk near line 396). `recordStop` increments the count when `asked` is true (head lines 2582-2588). `ClusterOnboardingFollowedStop` and `ClusterOnboardingStopped.asked(since:now:)` give the joining Mac a way to tell a person-requested stop from the start's own stop. Control messages gain `stopsBefore` and `serve(unlessStoppedSince:)`, which are visible only in the truncated patch excerpt.

Security-relevant observations:
- The counter is an integer in a local owner-controlled setup record and in the existing authenticated cable control channel. Nothing here touches the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), A-001 prompt data, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011) or key material.
- Stop handling (`localStop`, lines 2592-2625) keeps its existing ordering. The stop request is recorded, the local part is drained, then the peer is asked to stop. The guard at 2611 still fails closed if the record changed during the drain.
- `asked(since:now:)` returns false when either count is nil, so an older leader or an unreadable status never fabricates a stop. A lower count resets the baseline. A malicious peer on the control link could report a higher count to end the other Mac's follow, or hold the count back to keep a start from being stopped. That is a UX and availability effect on an already-trusted paired peer, and the peer can already issue stop commands over this channel, so I see no new privilege.
- `serveUnlessStopped` and `stopsBefore` are only in the truncated patch; I could not verify whether `localServe(unlessStoppedSince:)` rejects a stale or attacker-supplied `stopsBefore` safely. A wrong value could at worst skip or force a serve, which is a local availability matter.
- Diagnostics redaction (`saveDiagnostics`) is unchanged, and the new counter holds no identifiers.

Open integration questions: the implementation of `localServe(unlessStoppedSince:)`, and whether `stopsAsked` is bounded or validated on decode (overflow handling, `now > before`). I found no concrete regression.
